population.text: 88 patients with PKU who had responded to Kuvan in Study 1 (an open-label trial in patients ages 8 to 48 years with baseline blood Phe levels >= 450 µmol/L not on Phe-restricted diets)

citations.quote: Study 2 was a multicenter, double-blind, placebo-controlled study of 88 patients with PKU who responded to Kuvan in Study 1.

Study 1 was a multicenter, open-label, uncontrolled clinical trial of 489 patients with PKU, ages 8 to 48 years (mean 22 years), who had baseline blood Phe levels \ge 450 µmol/L and who were not on Phe-restricted diets.

endpoint.text: Mean change in blood Phe level from baseline to Week 6 in the Kuvan-treated group compared with the placebo group

citations.quote: Efficacy was assessed by the mean change in blood Phe level from baseline to Week 6 in the Kuvan-treated group as compared to the mean change in the placebo group.
Study 2 was a multicenter, double-blind, placebo-controlled study of 88 patients with PKU who responded to Kuvan in Study 1.
After a washout period from Study 1, patients were randomized equally to either Kuvan 10 mg/kg/day (N=41) or placebo (N=47) for 6 weeks.

result.text: At Week 6, mean change in blood Phe was -239 µmol/L with Kuvan versus 6 µmol/L with placebo (mean percent changes -29% and 3%); the between-group difference was statistically significant (p < 0.001)

citations.quote: At Week 6, the Kuvan- and placebo-treated groups had mean changes in blood Phe level of -239 and 6 µmol/L, respectively (mean percent changes of -29% (\pm 32) and 3% (\pm 33), respectively). The difference between the groups was statistically significant (p < 0.001) (Table 2).

indication.text: Kuvan is indicated to reduce blood phenylalanine (Phe) levels in patients with hyperphenylalaninemia (HPA) due to tetrahydrobiopterin- (BH4-) responsive Phenylketonuria (PKU), to be used in conjunction with a Phe-restricted diet

citations.quote: Kuvan™ is indicated to reduce blood phenylalanine (Phe) levels in patients with hyperphenylalaninemia (HPA) due to tetrahydrobiopterin- (BH4-) responsive Phenylketonuria (PKU). Kuvan is to be used in conjunction with a Phe-restricted diet.

target_moa.text: Kuvan is a synthetic form of BH4, the cofactor for phenylalanine hydroxylase (PAH); treatment with BH4 can activate residual PAH enzyme, improve oxidative metabolism of Phe, and decrease Phe levels in some patients

citations.quote: Kuvan is a synthetic form of BH4, the cofactor for the enzyme phenylalanine hydroxylase (PAH).
Treatment with BH4 can activate residual PAH enzyme, improve the normal oxidative metabolism of Phe, and decrease Phe levels in some patients.

modality.text: Small molecule (synthetic form of BH4, the cofactor tetrahydrobiopterin)

citations.quote: Kuvan is a synthetic form of BH4, the cofactor for the enzyme phenylalanine hydroxylase (PAH).

key_safety.text: Most common adverse reactions (>= 4% across all studies, n=579) were headache, diarrhea, abdominal pain, upper respiratory tract infection, pharyngolaryngeal pain, vomiting, and nausea; in controlled trials headache occurred in 15% (vs 14% placebo) and upper respiratory tract infection in 12% (vs 24% placebo). Mild to moderate neutropenia occurred in 24 of 579 patients (4%); most serious reactions were gastritis, spinal cord injury, streptococcal infection, testicular carcinoma, and urinary tract infection

citations.quote: The most common (\ge 4\% of patients treated with Kuvan) across all studies (n=579) were headache, diarrhea, abdominal pain, upper respiratory tract infection, pharyngolaryngeal pain, vomiting, and nausea.
Headache	11 (15)	8 (14)
Upper respiratory tract infection	9 (12)	14 (24)
Mild to moderate neutropenia was noted during Kuvan administration in 24 of 579 patients (4%).

The most serious adverse reactions during Kuvan administration (regardless of relationship to treatment) were gastritis, spinal cord injury, streptococcal infection, testicular carcinoma, and urinary tract infection.

detail.text: No companion diagnostic; response to Kuvan cannot be pre-determined by laboratory testing (e.g., genetic testing) and can only be determined by a therapeutic trial

citations.quote: it is not possible to accurately predict the extent of response before administering Kuvan to the patient, and response to treatment cannot be pre-determined by laboratory testing (e.g., genetic testing). Response to Kuvan can only be determined by a therapeutic trial.

requirement.text: Design, implement and complete a safety, efficacy, and pharmacokinetics study with Kuvan in patients with PKU four years of age or younger at study entry, with efficacy assessed by blood phenylalanine levels over a six-month treatment period

citations.quote: - BioMarin commits to designing and implementing a safety, efficacy, and pharmacokinetics study with Kuvan (sapropterin dihydrochloride) in patients with PKU who are four years of age or younger at study entry. Efficacy is to be assessed by the pharmacodynamic outcome measure of blood phenylalanine levels over a six-month period of treatment. A study protocol will be submitted to CDER by June 14, 2008, for concurrence, and the study will be initiated by December 14, 2008. The final study report for this study will be submitted to CDER by June 14, 2010.

requirement.text: Complete the open-label extension study PKU-008 in subjects with phenylketonuria who participated in studies PKU-004 or PKU-006

citations.quote: - BioMarin commits to completing the open-label extension study PKU-008, entitled "A Phase 3b, Multicenter, Open-Label Extension Study of Phenoptin™ in Subjects with Phenylketonuria Who Participated in Studies PKU-004 or PKU-006".1 Patients who participated in the extension study PKU-004 will be treated under PKU-008 for a minimum of two years of total treatment with Kuvan (sapropterin dihydrochloride).
